key_insight: An agent can reuse and iteratively refine an experimental strategy across different quantum processors to achieve the same quantum task despite device-specific differences and drift.
engineering_relevance: This points toward scalable, semi-automated quantum experimentation where human operators handle setup while an agent adapts control and measurement workflows across hardware platforms.
method: Developed an agent-assisted workflow on one three-qubit NMR processor and transferred it sequentially to four others.
Agent evaluated experimental evidence, chose the next measurements, and adapted procedures while operators handled preparation and physical intervention.
Applied the workflow to three-qubit Grover state preparation with device-specific calibration, pulse optimization, and measurement on each processor.
evidence_signal: Across four processors, the reconstructed dominant eigenstates had marked-state populations from 0.910 to 0.959, staying within 3.8% of the ideal 0.945.
watch_item: The approach still depends on human intervention for instrument preparation and hardware-specific adjustments, so full autonomy is not yet demonstrated.
paper_title: Agent-assisted experimental strategy transfer across quantum processors
